summary: Grays Harbor state tower: 50-ft pole tower (1948), 40-ft L-4 tower (1952), destroyed or removed 1973; a 2016 visit found no footings and a permit is required.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden L-4 tower with a 14x14 foot cab (1952), replacing a 1948 50-foot pole tower
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in 1973 (the registry says removed); a 2016 visit found a survey reference mark, not the cement footings earlier reports describe

access.note: As of 2016 Weyerhaeuser requires a permit: the Artic Permit, or the Aberdeen General Access Permit for February 1 to July 31

visit.trail_note: Gravel road to the summit; the last quarter mile was overgrowing in 2016

events.note: State Division of Forestry lookout: a 50-foot pole tower with a 12x12 foot slant-walled cab
Replaced by a 40-foot wooden L-4 tower with a 14x14 foot cab
Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station on the summit; Willhite found its reference mark in 2016
Tower and cab destroyed, per firelookout.com, Washington Lookouts and Willhite; the registry says it was removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com, Washington Lookouts and Willhite say the 1952 tower was destroyed in 1973; the registry says it was removed in 1973. The record uses 1973 with destroyed as the main event.

notes_for_editor: The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before the search step, so the story rests on the four cited pages only. No staffing or notable fires appear in these sources, so no staffing key is set. The brief's height_m 12.2 is the 1952 L-4 tower; the 1948 pole tower was 50 feet. Access level permission comes from the 2016 trip report and may have changed since. No photos were added.
